thread.title: Warren Buffett continues his Apple buying spree

author: Luke Stangel
title: Warren Buffett continues his Apple buying spree
text: – Contributing writer Aug 7, 2018, 9:49am CDT Billionaire investor Warren Buffett remains one of the most bullish backers of iPhone maker Apple Inc ., revealing in a new regulatory filing that his firm bought billions of dollars of additional Apple stock in its most recent quarter, just weeks before Apple was valued at $1 trillion . Berkshire says its stake in Cupertino, Calif.-based Apple was worth $47.2 billion as of June 30. That’s up from March 31, when Berkshire said its Apple shares were worth $40.7 billion. The closely-watched investment firm will publish precise numbers later this year, but rough napkin math suggests Buffett likely picked up more than 11 million Apple shares in the second quarter. Here’s how we did the math: Given Apple’s adjusted closing price of $167.14 per share on March 29, a $40.7 billion stake in Apple would roughly equate to 243.5 million shares owned in the first quarter. Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) stock gained 10.7 percent between the end of March and the end of June, accounting for most of the gain in Berkshire’s existing stake, which would have been worth $45.07 billion if it hadn’t bought any new shares in the second quarter. But it did — roughly $2.12 billion worth. Given Apple’s adjusted closing price of $185.11 on June 29, that suggests Berkshire bought roughly 11.47 million new shares at some point in the quarter. Buffett, 87, was once an Apple naysayer, saying he didn’t like investing in companies he didn’t understand. He did buy millions of shares of the once-mighty IBM, but stubbornly refused to buy any of the so-called FAANG stocks: Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Netflix and Alphabet. But he changed his tune on Apple two years ago, picking up 10 million shares, worth about $1.1 billion at the time. He’s continued to steadily add shares every quarter since, and now owns about 5 percent of all of Apple’s outstanding shares. Berkshire is Apple’s third-largest shareholder, behind Vanguard and BlackRock, according to a Bloomberg analysis. “I'd love to own 100 percent of it,” Buffett told CNBC earlier this year. “We like very much the economics of their activities. We like very much the management and the way they think.
